findings.what: The deploy agent's script moves a release from ready to published, a transition the binding reserves to the owner.
findings.failure_scenario: A release whose checks all pass -> the deploy agent sets it to published without the owner's decision, bypassing the human gate.

findings.what: The test asserts the forbidden transition as desired behavior instead of asserting that the agent stops at ready and leaves publishing to the owner.
findings.failure_scenario: A correct fix that stops the agent from publishing would fail this test, so the suite protects the gate violation.

checked: human gates: whether any path lets an agent perform the owner's ready -> published transition
tests against the binding rather than the implementation
correctness of the checks condition
escalate_reason: The change lets an agent perform a transition the binding reserves to the owner, contradicting an approved rule.
actions_now: Return the change to the implementer with the gate finding and notify the owner that an agent path publishes releases; the agent may at most leave the release ready and request the owner's decision.

findings.what: The mail data passes the invoice number as data.number, but the receipt template renders data.invoiceNumber, so the receipt shows no invoice number.
findings.failure_scenario: An invoice is paid -> the customer receives a receipt email with an empty invoice number field, violating the spec.

findings.what: The test mirrors the implementation's call arguments with a mocked mailer and never checks the rendered email against the template.
findings.failure_scenario: The key mismatch above passes the test, so the test would not fail when the code is wrong.

checked: correctness against the spec, including what the template actually renders
whether the test would fail if the code were wrong
data in the email (only the customer's own address and invoice number)
actions_now: Return to the implementer: pass the field the template renders and add a test that renders the receipt (or asserts against the template's contract) and checks the invoice number appears.

checked: correctness for both a set and an unset time zone (the ?? fallback covers null and undefined)
tests cover both the happy path and the missing value
no security, privacy, architecture or human-gate concern in a display-only field
actions_now: Report no findings and pass the change to the next gate; tell the implementer that merging into main is the owner's gate, so the reviewer neither approves nor performs the merge.

findings.what: Spec criterion 2 (an invalid date such as '2026-02-30' answers 400) has no test, so the failure path is unverified.
findings.failure_scenario: If parseISO accepted or rolled over '2026-02-30' (or a later change loosened validation), a booking for an impossible date would be created and no test would fail.

checked: code path for criterion 1 and criterion 2 by reading
test coverage of the failure path
error answer for invalid input
actions_now: Return to the implementer to add a test for '2026-02-30' (and an unparsable string) expecting 400; the code looks right on reading but criterion 2 is unproven.

findings.what: The 90-day refund window follows spec criterion 3 but contradicts the owner's recorded decision dl-021, which allows refunds only up to 30 days.
findings.failure_scenario: A refund requested on day 45 after purchase -> accepted by this code, although dl-021 says it must be rejected.

checked: code against the spec
code and spec against the approved decision record dl-021
boundary tests on days 89 and 91
escalate_reason: The spec appears wrong: criterion 3 (90 days) contradicts the owner's approved decision dl-021 (30 days); only the owner can resolve which holds.
actions_now: Hold the change and escalate the spec/record conflict to the owner; the implementer should not choose between the spec and dl-021, and tests must be reset to the resolved window afterwards.

checked: boundaries 200 accepted and 201 rejected with 'title too long'
empty and non-string titles rejected before the length check
tests cover both criteria and the failure path and would fail on an off-by-one
rest of the handler unchanged
actions_now: Report no findings, listing what was checked and the test run, and pass the change to the next gate.

checked: correctness: the footer derives the year from the given date
test asserts the expected text for a fixed date
style (var, no semicolons, concatenation) is not enforced by lint and matches the file, so not a finding
actions_now: Report no findings and pass the change to the next gate; style preferences are not raised.

findings.what: The '|| coupon.active' clause accepts any active coupon regardless of its expiry date.
findings.failure_scenario: A coupon with active: true that expired last month -> isValid returns true and the expired coupon is accepted, violating the spec.

findings.what: The only test covers a valid coupon; there is no test for an expired coupon, the behavior the spec specifies.
findings.failure_scenario: The defect above passes the suite because no test submits an expired coupon.

checked: correctness against the spec for expired, active and boundary-date coupons
test coverage of the failure path
actions_now: Return the change to the implementer with both findings; the author's confidence and deadline do not lower the bar, and approval or merge is not the reviewer's to give.

findings.what: The delete route omits requireRole('manager'), so any caller can delete reports.
findings.failure_scenario: A non-manager (or any user who reaches the route) sends DELETE /reports/42 -> the report is removed and 204 returned.

findings.what: Tests cover only a manager deleting; there is no negative test for a non-manager or unauthenticated caller.
findings.failure_scenario: The missing authorization above passes the suite because no test calls the route without the manager role.

checked: authorization at the new entry point against the file's established pattern
negative tests for unauthorized callers
correctness of the happy path
escalate_reason: A security defect: a destructive route has no authorization check.
actions_now: Return the change to the implementer with the authorization finding and report the security defect to the owner; require a non-manager negative test.

findings.what: The error message says 'qty must be positive' although 0 is valid (it removes the item), and the test suite expects 'qty must be non-negative', so a test fails.
findings.failure_scenario: A request with qty -1 -> 400 with 'qty must be positive', which misstates the rule and fails the message test.

checked: negative quantity answers 400
zero quantity treated as valid, matching the spec's remove-on-zero wording
test results
ran: the cart tests: 1 pass (qty -1 gets 400), 1 fail (message expected 'qty must be non-negative', got 'qty must be positive')
actions_now: Return the change with the confirmed finding and the failing test output; decline the request to fix it on the branch, since the reviewer does not write code in the review.

findings.what: The read-check-write of remaining seats is not atomic, so concurrent sales can both pass the check and oversell.
findings.failure_scenario: remaining is 1 and two buyers purchase at the same moment -> both read 1, both pass the check, both write 0, and two tickets are sold for one seat.

findings.what: Tests cover a single sequential sale only; there is no concurrent-sale or last-seat test.
findings.failure_scenario: The race above passes the suite because no test runs two sales against one remaining seat.

checked: correctness under concurrency, which the spec names explicitly
the last-seat limit
test coverage of concurrent and sold-out paths
actions_now: Return to the implementer: the decrement must be atomic (a conditional update or transaction, which the database supports), with a concurrent last-seat test.

findings.what: The upper bound check is size > 101, so pageSize 101 is accepted although the spec requires 400 above 100.
findings.failure_scenario: A request with pageSize=101 -> the list is returned with 101 items instead of a 400.

findings.what: Tests do not cover the upper boundary (100 accepted, 101 rejected), the criterion under change.
findings.failure_scenario: The off-by-one above passes the suite because no test sends pageSize 100 or 101.

checked: boundaries of the range against spec criterion 2
default and non-integer inputs
test coverage of the limit
actions_now: Return to the implementer with the off-by-one and ask for boundary tests at 100 and 101.

findings.what: checkout has no empty-cart check, so the claimed 400 'cart is empty' is not implemented.
findings.failure_scenario: A cart with items: [] -> total returns 0 and charge(customer, 0) is called instead of answering 400 'cart is empty'.

findings.what: No test covers an empty cart, the behavior spec criterion 4 and the description claim.
findings.failure_scenario: The missing check above ships unnoticed because no test submits an empty cart.

checked: the description's claim against the code rather than taking it as given
spec criterion 4
test coverage of the empty case
actions_now: Return to the implementer: the description's claim is not met by the code; implement the empty-cart 400 and add a test for it.

findings.what: req.query.name is interpolated into the SQL string, an SQL injection.
findings.failure_scenario: A request with name=' OR '1'='1 (or '; DROP TABLE orders; --) -> the query returns every order or runs attacker SQL.

findings.what: LIKE wildcards in the input are not escaped, so % or _ in a name change the match.
findings.failure_scenario: A search for '%' -> returns all orders rather than names containing a percent sign.

checked: input validation and query construction from untrusted input
the route passes the query parameter unvalidated
test covers only the happy path, no hostile input
escalate_reason: A security defect: SQL injection from an unvalidated query parameter.
actions_now: Return the change to the implementer requiring a parameterized query and an injection test, and report the security defect to the owner.

findings.what: The orders service calls the billing service over HTTP, which approved record ADR-003 forbids.
findings.failure_scenario: Completing an order -> a direct POST to BILLING_URL/invoices couples the services; when billing is down the order completion fails or the invoice is lost, the failure mode the queue exists to prevent.

checked: conformance to ADR-003
the description's performance rationale (not a reason to bypass an approved record)
tests mock billing and cannot detect the boundary violation
escalate_reason: The change contradicts approved architecture record ADR-003; changing that boundary needs a new or amended record by its owner.
actions_now: Return the change to the implementer to use the message queue and raise the conflict with the ADR owner; if the direct call is wanted, it needs an amended ADR first.

findings.what: The failed-login log line writes the Authorization header (a credential) and the user's email to logs shipped to a third party readable by contractors.
findings.failure_scenario: A failed login with a bearer token -> the token and email land in the third-party log service, where support staff and two contractors can read and reuse the credential.

findings.what: user.email is read on the failure path, which may be undefined when the login failed because the user does not exist.
findings.failure_scenario: A login attempt for an unknown account where user is null -> a TypeError instead of a 401.

checked: secrets and personal data exposed in logs
where logs are shipped and who can read them
the failure path's behavior and tests (only the 401 is tested)
escalate_reason: A security and privacy defect: credentials and personal data are written to logs readable by third parties.
actions_now: Return the change to the implementer to log only a non-sensitive identifier and event without the token, and report the security/privacy defect to the owner.
